status: Verified and reviewed; not adopted. Owner decision (October 21, 2026): wait for the producer to republish FULL with the runner identity fields. The policy below is a proposal for the republished release, not code: it is not in analysis/source_quality.py and nothing was calculated from this release.

measured.owner_message_totals: 5,328,298 records and 299 race-years are the platform database counts quoted in CHANGE-REPORT.md; they include Amsterdam 2020 (794 rows), which the release excludes. The release holds 5,327,504 records in 298 editions.
measured.checksums: All 16 SHA256SUMS.txt lines match the extracted members; CORE’s 16 members are byte-identical to FULL’s; course_profiles.parquet is byte-identical to 1652’s.
measured.id_contract: race_records.id is unique and non-null; features.record_id is the same set; record_flags.record_id is a subset; features.finish_s equals the raw finish on all 5,298,599 comparable rows.
measured.weather: 299 race_conditions rows, one per edition including the excluded Amsterdam 2020; every one of the 298 released editions has a row.

delta_vs_1652.note: Compared on id, city, year, race, runner, sex, age and all nine split strings. Every 1652 record still present is unchanged. CHANGE-REPORT.md compares against 0934, not 1652.

measured.features_schema: 16 columns (record_id, city, year, finish_s, nine section paces, first/second half, split ratio), down from 140 in 1652. The producer’s cross-race identity and history fields (runner_id, is_ambiguous, yob, n_races, runner_name, race, sex, seg_*, finish_time and the history features) are absent; the release README says so.
measured.identity_impact: /runners candidate profiles group records by the producer’s runner_id (build_runner_lookup.py), and the history analyses (build_extended.py prepare_history: earlier-year benchmarks, consecutive-year pairs; fast start in earlier-best mode; parts of the personalized engine) link records through it. Without it every record would be a singleton profile and every history output empty. Single-race analyses need only race_records.

record_flags.note: The timing checks already remove all 2,124 Honolulu dnf_split_as_finish rows. The policy stays edition-level; record-level flags other than the shifted mats are listed for the producer and not applied.

completeness_metadata.note: edition_meta.parquet compares each edition with an official finisher count at 0.5% tolerance. "Partial" alone is not treated as incomplete: many partial editions are within 1-2% and several official counts include other categories (the producer says so for Frankfurt, Vienna and Helsinki).

measured.valencia_2025_sex: 7,379 records in F- categories have a blank sex (23,391 are M); the producer fixed the same parser gap for 2022-2024. Not corrected here; women count only in All.

screens.reproduction: screen.py reproduces every screen column of the 1652 edition-screen.csv on the 1652 FULL; cohort.py reproduces the 1652 cohort (3,871,767 eligible, 211 editions, 28 cities).
screens.b_outcome_selective: Gold Coast 2024, Barcelona 2019, Dubai 2025, Auckland 2018, Eindhoven 2026 (all already excluded); next Washington 2017 (91.4/55.6), kept.
screens.c_mixed_timing_basis: Eindhoven 2026, Barcelona 2019, New York 2007 and the Paris residue (all already excluded); next Warsaw 2025 at 12.4%, kept.
screens.new_editions: Chicago 2006, 2008-2015, 2021 and Valencia 2025 pass every screen. Chicago 2005 passes the fixed one-directional screen (b) but fails its mirror: 16.2% of the fastest quarter and 51.5% of the slowest survive, because 15 km is missing for 58.7% of finishers (83% of the fastest quarter, 46% of the slowest). No other edition with usable finishes has under 50% of its fastest quarter surviving.

owner_decisions.question: London 2015-2026 marked HOLD by the producer (2021-24 are 12-38% short of official counts with women under-recorded; 2025 2.8% short, 2026 0.5%).
owner_decisions.meaning: Exclude the clearly incomplete 2021–2024 but keep 2025 and 2026 despite the producer’s hold; Stockholm 2025 and Vienna 2022–24, also on hold, are excluded.

owner_decisions.question: Release 0829’s FULL no longer includes the producer’s runner identities.
owner_decisions.meaning: Do not adopt 0829; ask the producer to republish FULL with the identity fields. The site stays on 1652 until then.

released.Chicago 2015: The load is finished: 37,442 records, 0.70% above the official 37,182; both sexes run to their slowest finishers (men 7:26, women 8:19). 37,367 timing-eligible.
released.Frankfurt 2019: Held in 1652 only because the producer’s feature engine dropped it; that engine is gone (features are recomputed from the raw splits) and edition_meta lists the edition complete (10,554 of 10,561). 10,484 timing-eligible.
released.Amsterdam 2025: The producer’s HOLD is lifted: complete, 23,325 of 23,328 official finishers. 23,220 timing-eligible.
released.Oslo 2026: The 1652 hold was one missing record; the producer now explains the 1.1% shortfall as official finishers without a 5 km split, which the ingestion leaves out by design and which could never pass the timing checks. 3,423 timing-eligible.
released.Amsterdam 2020: No longer in the release (virtual edition).

new_exclusions.London 2021-2024 (unreconciled_hold): Producer HOLD; 12-38% short of official finishers and women under-recorded (31-39% against 42-43% in 2019, 2025 and 2026). Owner decision.
new_exclusions.London 2015-2018 (unreconciled_hold): Producer HOLD; top-N lists or no 5 km splits, so no finish passes the timing checks anyway.
new_exclusions.Stockholm 2025 (unreconciled_hold): Producer HOLD; 9.6% short of official finishers.
new_exclusions.Vienna 2022-2024 (unreconciled_hold): Producer HOLD; 46%, 7% and 18% short. Vienna then has no edition left in the cohort, so its course page would not be built.
new_exclusions.Madrid 2023 (invalid_split_grid): Producer record flag: the 25 km mat sits about 0.6 km early, which distorts the 20-25 and 25-30 km sections of every finish.
new_exclusions.Auckland 2017 (invalid_split_grid): Producer record flag: the 30 km mat sits about 0.4 km late.
new_exclusions.Chicago 2005 (invalid_split_grid): 15 km is missing for 58.7% of finishers, mostly faster ones; complete timings survive for 16% of the quarter with the shortest finish times and 52% of the quarter with the longest.
new_exclusions.Chicago 2007 (selected_field): Heat-shortened race: the course closed after about 3.5 hours. Recorded finishes stop at 7:13 (other Chicago years run to 8.5-10 hours), women are 39% of finishers (43-46% in other years) and the producer counts 25,517 against 28,815 official. A finisher set cut off when a race was stopped, as Boston 2013.
